target_customer: Drivers on smartphones at first, then automakers and suppliers wanting AR navigation in vehicle displays
problem: Turn by turn maps are hard to match to the real road. Phiar used on-device computer vision to overlay navigation on the live camera view.
business_model: Consumer app at first, later B2B software licensing to automakers

founders.name: Chen-Ping Yu
education: PhD Computer Science, Stony Brook University
founders.background_notes: YC page cites over 10 years of computer vision research. A podcast summary says the idea came from wrong turns in Boston and names Ivy Li as co-founder, but I did not open that source, so she is not recorded as a founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running real time road understanding on phone grade compute needed deep learning and AR research, rare for a small team in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Company materials claim patented deep learning and AR methods, but large mapping firms could build similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mapbox shipped a Vision SDK for AR navigation and Google Maps added Live View AR. Google then acquired Phiar in 2022, whose CEO had previously led Google's Android Automotive platforms.

market_need_then: Navigation errors and distraction are common driver complaints and in 2018 to 2019 phone AR was emerging. No spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: phiar.net, not a .com; that host did not resolve from this environment.

rebrands.why: Company moved from the iPhone beta toward automaker partnerships such as Qualcomm in 2021; no formal rename was found

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, VentureBeat and several podcasts, mostly about technology rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Good tech press for the seed and Series A, but no brand-specific assets and a hard to say name.

pivots.from: Smartphone AR navigation app for drivers
pivots.to: B2B AR navigation software for automakers and in-vehicle displays
pivots.why: Qualcomm partnership and a Series A with automotive investors and an ex-Google automotive CEO

outcome_analysis: Phiar was a research heavy startup that raised a 3 million dollar seed in 2018 and a 12 million dollar Series A in 2021 from automotive investors, hiring a former Google Android Automotive head as CEO. It shifted from a phone app to selling software to automakers and was acquired by Google in 2022 on undisclosed terms. The deep learning on-device capability and the automotive pivot are the visible reasons for the exit.
notes: Seed size conflicts: headlines say 3 million while The Bridge lists 2.5 million plus about 200 thousand angel money; 3 million is recorded from the 2018 headlines. Acquisition date conflicts: YC page news says December 2022 while The Bridge article is dated 2022-09-22 with an acquired headline, and CB Insights dates a headline 2023-09; only the year is recorded. Series A lead conflicts (State Farm Ventures per The Bridge, Cambridge Mobile Telematics per SeedTable). A search snippet listed Zoom Ventures, which no source supports. Phiar.net did not resolve here. A dated 2018 competitor search found Mapbox Vision SDK and a 2019 market report but no clearly dated 2018 source, so the list is empty. The pivot date is approximate.
